hr_greeting.ai_message:
Good morning, Ana Lucía.

One assignment. Human Resources — Salary and Benefits, 14 questions, due September 30.

No inbox. No attachment. No forwarded link. And nothing from any other office or any other school — you see what you own, when you need it.

It is open in front of you. Stop halfway if you need to; nothing is lost.
suggested_chips: Ask the other schools a question

hr_reopen.ai_message:
Here it is, exactly where you left it.

Work through it and submit when you are ready — I will show you your own figures the moment AMISA has them.
suggested_chips: Ask the other schools a question

hr_definition.ai_message:
Base salary only. It excludes housing, benefits, allowances and bonuses, and it is expressed as a full-time equivalent annual amount in USD.

That definition sits beside the question itself, so you are not guessing — and neither is the school in Guatemala, or the one in Brazil.

Comparability is won at the point of entry, not in the analysis.
suggested_chips: Ask the other schools a question

hr_submitted.ai_message:
Submitted, timestamped and logged.

Here is your own salary structure, charted. For a school with no warehouse and no analyst, this is the first time it has been visible in one place.

Notice what is not here: no benchmark, no peer group, no other school. The window is still open. Nothing compares until the association closes the wave.
suggested_chips: Ask the other schools a question

hr_request.user_query: Ask the other schools a question
hr_request.ai_message:
Your head of school wants to ask the membership about kindergarten wait lists and planned tuition increases.

Four questions. You do not email 70 people — it goes to AMISA first, which is the control the association keeps.

hr_request_sent.ai_message:
Sent to the Executive Director.

Nothing reaches the other schools until he approves it. If he does, it goes out with a window, reminders and a completion rate — instead of living in an inbox where half the membership never sees it.
